questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a university with good academic opportunities and still live fairly close to the water to go surfing in my free time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any problems finding information I needed upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an introduction lecture for exchange students get the information we needed. Also there were a day in the first week where all the societies of the university had stalls and told about what they did. It was fx the surf society, diving society or the QUEST society, which is a society for international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy for me because I looked before hand. However I know people who ended up paying quite a lot because they hadn't looked before.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The UQ campus is outside a bit outside the city center, so I enjoyed living off campus to be closer to the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I managed to get a fairly cheap place to stay in West End of Brisbane which is a very nice part of the city. However I know a lot of people who had to live in quite expensive student accommodation. I would say that it is worthwhile looking for accommodation before arriving. I myself lived in Westella, a student accommodation for 22 students with shared kitchens and bathrooms.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You first had to enroll in courses. To be able to enroll in a course you also needed to get pre approval of the host university. It is possible to enroll in 5 courses and then later drop one of them, when you have figured out which 4 you would like. After enrolling you could choose at what time you wanted practicals and tutorials. I would recommend to do this as soon as possible to have as many options available as possible.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There where both a consultation where staff from the different faculties helped with pre approval and the student services could also help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got to register to all the 5 classes I wanted whereafter I dropped one of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It helped me to look at programs that were similar to my own to get inspiration for courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 2 second year economic courses, 1 second year math course and a first year history course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar with 1 lecture pr week and 1-2 tutorials or practicals.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON2020 - Intermediate Macroeconomics
ECON2300 - Introductory Econometrics
MATH2504 - Programming for Mathematicians
HIST1201 - The Australian Experience

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The Programming for Mathematicians is one of the best courses I have done so far. However it was also very challenging, especially in the start.
I would also recommend The Australian Experience which was a history course about Australian history. I very much enjoyed trying a different type of course than mathematics or economics that I am used to.

Food DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was a lot more expensive than what I thought. Also compared to Denmark. Public transport however is very cheap in Brisbane.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds both different kind of sports, societies such as the UQ Surfers who did weekend trips and the QUEST society who arranged trips and bar nights for international students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend the QUEST society and the UQ Surfers.
Also I would also recommend the UNIDIVE - The University of Queensland Underwater Club, which I didn't participate in myself. However I would very much have liked to go diving in the weekends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Noosa, Gold Coast and Byron Bay are great for weekend trips. Either to just go to the beach or go surfing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, the culture is not very different from the danish one.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly met local students at my classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The relaxed surfer culture here in Australia.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to also enjoy your freetime to go explore places in Australia.
Most of the assessment is due during the semester. Don't stress about this too much. It also makes the examination period less stresfull.
Look forward for your stay!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being within two hours drive of some very beautiful nature and surfspots.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first assignment of Programming for Mathematicians, was very challenging and time consuming.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
